entries.sanskrit:
अष्टमे नाम-कर्मास्य बाल-क्रीडा-कुतूहले ।

मृद्-भक्षणाभियोगे च विश्व-रूपं निरूप्यते ॥

विश्वरूपादि-बालस्य निशम्याशङ्किनः पितुः ।

नाम-कृद्-गर्ग-वाक्येन निजं तत्त्वम् असूसुचत् ॥
entries.literal_english: The eighth chapter concerns the naming ceremony, the child’s playful activities, the charge that He ate earth, and the revelation of the universal form. After hearing of that revelation and the other childhood events, the anxious father receives knowledge of the child’s true nature through Garga’s words.

entries.sanskrit: पूर्णश् चेत् कथं धनिनां गृहम् आगतस् तत्राह---महद्-विचलनम् इति । महतां स्वाश्रमाद् अन्यत्र विचलनं न स्वार्थं किन्तु गृहिणां मङ्गलाय । ननु तर्हि स एव महद्-दर्शनार्थं किम् इति नागच्छन्ति तत्राह । दीन-चेतसां कृपणानां क्षणम् अपि गृहं त्यक्तुम् अशक्नुवताम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४॥
entries.literal_english: If Garga is complete and self-sufficient, why did he come to the house of the wealthy? Śrīdhara answers that a great person’s leaving his own āśrama is not for personal gain but for the welfare of householders. Why, then, do the poor not go to see such great people? Their minds are pitiable because they cannot leave their homes even for a moment.

entries.sanskrit:
त्वया बालयोर् नाम-करणादि करणीयम् इति वक्तुं तस्य ज्ञानातिशयम् आह---ज्योतिषाम् अयनम् इति । यद् अतीन्द्रिय-ज्ञानम् असाधनं ज्योतिषाम् अयनं तत्-प्रतिपादकं ज्योतिः-शास्त्रम् इत्य् अर्थः । तत् साक्षाद् भवता प्रणीतं येन अन्योऽपि पुमान् परावरं परं कारणं पूर्व-जन्म-कृतं कर्म अवरं कार्यं तस्मिन् जन्मनि भावि-फलं तद् वेद । उक्तं च जातके---

 यद् उपचितम् अन्य-जन्मनि शुभाशुभं तस्य कर्मणः पङ्क्तिम् ।
 व्यञ्जयति शास्त्रम् एतत् तमसि द्रञाणि दीप इव ॥ इति ॥५॥
word_for_word: karma done in a former birth
entries.literal_english: To show that Garga should perform the naming and other rites, Śrīdhara describes his exceptional knowledge. He is the foundation of astrology, meaning the science that reveals knowledge beyond the senses. It was directly composed by him, and through it a person can know the supreme prior cause, the karma accumulated in former births, and the future result in the present birth. The traditional comparison is that the science reveals the sequence of good and bad deeds from another birth like a lamp reveals objects in darkness.

entries.sanskrit: विवक्षितम् आह---त्वं हीति । दैवज्ञो मन्त्रविच् च त्वम् अतो नाम-करणादि-संस्कारान् कर्तुम् अर्हसीत्य् अर्थः । नन्व् एतद् गुरुणा करणीयम् इति चेत् तत्राह---नॄणाम् इति ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: The intended meaning is: you are a knower of astrology and of mantras; therefore you are qualified to perform the naming and other saṃskāras. If one objects that these rites should be done by the family guru, Śrīdhara answers by referring to the rites prescribed for human beings.

entries.sanskrit: अत्युत्साहिनं नन्दं प्रति गुप्तम् एतत्-कार्यम् इत्य् अभिप्रायेण प्रत्याचक्षाण इवाह---सुतम् इति । कंसो मन्यते मन्येत कल्पयेद् इत्य् अर्थः ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: Garga appears to refuse Nanda’s enthusiastic request because this work must remain secret. Kaṁsa may think that this is your son, and the naming rite would reveal too much.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: ननु यदु-कुमार इति कथञ्चिज् जानातु । तत्र वसुदेवस्य सुतस् तत्रापि देवक्यां जात इति कुतो जानीयात् तत्राह---पाप-मतिर् इत्य्-आदि ॥८॥
entries.literal_english: The question is: even if Kaṁsa somehow knows that the child is a Yadu prince, how could he know that He is Vasudeva’s son and was born to Devakī? Śrīdhara points to the explanation beginning with the words ‘evil-minded’; Kaṁsa’s suspicion is rooted in that wicked understanding.

entries.sanskrit: किं मया हतया मन्द इत्य्-आदि देवकी-कन्या-वचः श्रुत्वा, देवक्या अष्टमो गर्भो न स्त्री भवितुम् अर्हति इति नित्यं सञ्चिन्तयन् सामान्येन क्वचिद् अस्तीति ज्ञात्वा युवयोश् च सख्यं सञ्चिन्तयंस् त्वद्-गृहे भवेद् इति सम्भाव्य मत्-संस्कार-लिङ्गेन चागताशङ्क आगता आशङ्का यस्य सः । अपि यदि हन्ता हनिष्यति, तर्हि तत् तदा नो महान् अनयः स्याद् इति ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: After hearing Devakī’s daughter say ‘what would be gained by killing me, foolish one?’, Kaṁsa constantly reflects that the eighth embryo of Devakī could not be a female. Knowing generally that the child must exist somewhere, thinking of the friendship between the two families and imagining that the child might be in your house, he becomes suspicious from the signs produced by his own rites and calculations. Even if the killer should kill Him, he reasons, then a great calamity would arise.

entries.sanskrit: द्विजाति-संस्कारं द्विजातीनाम् अवश्यं कर्तव्यं संस्कार-मात्रं केवलं स्वस्ति-वाचन-पूर्वकं कुर्विति ॥१०-११॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara takes the passage as prescribing the essential twice-born saṃskāra: perform only the rite that must be done for the twice-born, preceded by the recitation of auspicious blessings.

entries.sanskrit: यदूनाम् अपृथग्-भावात् कुतश्चिद् हेतोर् विप्रतिपद्यमानानां यदूनाम् अपृथग्-भावाद् भावो भावनं तस्मात् । अन्योन्य-शिक्षया सर्वैक-मत्य-करणाद् इत्य् अर्थः । सम्यक् कर्षत्य् एकीकरोतीति सङ्कर्षणम् अप्य् उशन्ति मन्यन्ते वक्ष्यन्तीत्य् अर्थः । गर्भ-सङ्कर्षणं तु न प्रकाशयति ॥१२॥
entries.literal_english: Because the Yadus are not separate from one another, the idea of unity is intended: they make one another of a single mind through mutual instruction. Saṅkarṣaṇa is also understood as ‘the one who draws together and unites.’ The transfer of the embryo is not revealed.

entries.literal_english: This is your son; therefore one name will be Kṛṣṇa.

entries.sanskrit: इतीति । इत्य् आत्मानं प्रति समादिश्य । आत्मानं कृष्णं च । गर्गे गते सति, आशिषाम् आशीर्भिः नन्दः पूर्णं विष्णुं मेने अमंस्त ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: Having instructed himself and Kṛṣṇa with the words ‘so be it,’ and after Garga had gone, Nanda considered Viṣṇu complete through the blessings he had received.

entries.sanskrit:
बाल-क्रीडा-चमत्कारैः कृष्णो रामेण संयुतः ।

परमानन्दम् आधत्त व्रजे नन्द-यशोदयोः ॥॥

पूर्णत्वम् एव दर्शयन्न् आह---कालेन इति ॥२१॥
entries.literal_english: Kṛṣṇa, together with Rāma, filled Nanda and Yaśodā with supreme bliss through the wonders of childhood play. Śrīdhara then shows His fullness by the word ‘in time.’

entries.sanskrit: तदा च तन्-मातरौ निज-सुतौ उपगुह्य दोर्भ्यां प्रमोदं ययतुः । कथम्-भूते ? घृणया कृपया स्नुवन्त्यौ पयः-पूर्ण-पयोधरे सत्यौ । पङ्केनाङ्ग-रागेण रुचिरौ । कथम्-भूतं मुखं निरीक्ष्य ? मुग्धं मन्दं स्मितं यस्मिन् अल्पा दशनाश् च यस्मिन्, तच् च तच् च ॥२३॥
entries.literal_english: At that time the two mothers embraced their own sons with their arms and became joyful. Their breasts were full of milk flowing from compassion; their bodies were beautiful with the unguent of earth or scented paste; and they gazed upon faces that were innocent, gently smiling and furnished with only a few teeth.

entries.sanskrit:
कृष्ण-चापल-चौर्याणि सहैवाखिल-सद्मतः ।

प्रजल्पन्त्यः समागत्य गोप्यो गोप्यै मुदं ददुः ॥॥

असमयेऽदोह-काले । क्रोशे सञ्जात-हासः सञ्जातो हासो यस्य सः । स्तेयं चौर्यार्जितं, न तु दत्तं । तत्रापि स्वादु नेतरत् दधि च पयश् चात्ति । किं च, भोक्ष्यन् मर्कान् मर्कटान् प्रति विभज्य ददाति, तेषां मध्ये तृप्तत्वेन कोऽपि नात्ति चेत्, तर्हि भाण्डं भिनत्ति । क्वचिद् द्रव्यस्यालाभे सति स गृहाय "धक्ष्यामि" इति कुपितो याति । यद् वा, स गृहा गृहिणः, तेभ्यः कुपितः, तेषां तोकान् बालान् पर्यङ्कादिषु सुप्तान् उपक्रोश्य रोदयित्वा यातीति ॥२९॥

कृष्ण-चापल-चौर्याणि सहैवाखिल-सद्मतः ।

प्रजल्पन्त्यः समागत्य गोप्यो गोप्यै मुदं ददुः ॥॥
word_for_word: when it was not milking time
entries.literal_english: The Gopīs gathered from every house and told one another of Kṛṣṇa’s mischief and theft, giving joy to the other women. He acted outside the proper milking time, and a cry of laughter arose. He ate the stolen yogurt and milk, not other foods; while eating, He distributed portions to the monkeys. If none of them became satisfied and ate, He broke the pot. When no item was available, He angrily went away threatening to burn the house. Alternatively, He became angry with the householders, woke their children sleeping on beds and made them cry before leaving.

entries.sanskrit: कल्पितैः स्तेय-योगैर् [२९] इत्य् उक्तं तत् प्रपञ्चयति---हस्ताग्राह्ये इति । तुङ्ग-शिक्य-स्थ-भाण्डेष्व् अन्तर्-निहिते दध्य्-आदौ वयुनं ज्ञानं यस्य स छिद्रं रचयति, तद्-विच्छिद्र-रचनादि-वित् । ध्वान्त-युक्ते गृहे स्वाङ्गम् एव अर्थं प्रदीपं रचयति विशेषतो धृत-मणि-गणम् । यर्हि यस्मिन् काले ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara now expands the devices of theft mentioned previously. When the butter and other food were hidden in pots hanging high beyond the hand’s reach, He knew where they were and made a hole. In a dark house He made His own body a lamp, especially by displaying the jewels He wore. ‘Yarhi’ means ‘at whatever time.’

entries.sanskrit: एवम् एतद् विचित्रं विश्वं सहैकदैव वीक्ष्य विचित्रताम् आह । जीवश् च गुण-क्षोभकः कालश् च परिणाम-हेतुः स्वभावश् च जन्म-हेतुः कर्म च तत्-संस्कार-भूतः आशयश् च एतैर् लिङ्गानां चराचर-शरीराणां भेदो यस्मिंस् तत् । तत्र व्रजं च सहात्मानं स्व-सहितं क्वचिद् वीक्ष्य सूनोस् तनाव् अल्पे विदारिते आस्ये शङ्काम् अवाप ॥३९॥
entries.literal_english: After seeing this strange universe all at once, Yaśodā describes its strangeness. The differences among moving and unmoving bodies arise from the jīva, which agitates the guṇas; time, which causes transformation; svabhāva, which causes birth; karma, which forms the impressions; and the āśaya, the deep disposition. Seeing Vraja together with herself inside the small opening of her son’s mouth, she became doubtful.

entries.sanskrit: ताम् एवाह---किं स्वप्नः ? इति । परितो विलोक्याह--नायं स्वप्नः । तर्हि किं देवस्य हरेर् माया ? इति । तथा चेद् अन्ये किं न पश्यन्ति ? तर्हि किं वा मदीय एव कश्चिद् बुद्धि-मोहो धी-विपर्यासो दर्पणे मुखवत् ? एवं तर्ह्य् अयं कृष्णोऽपि कथम् अन्तः प्रतीयते ? नहि दर्पणे दर्पण-प्रतीतिः । अन्तर् बहिश् चैक-रूपेण च कथं जगत् प्रतीयते ? तथा सति बिम्ब-प्रतिबिम्बयोर् इव परस्परं वैपरीत्येन प्रतीतिः स्याद् इत्य् आशङ्क्यान्यथा वितर्कयति---अथो इति । अथवा, मम एवामुष्य अर्भकस्यापि सतो यः कश्चन अचिन्त्य आत्म-योगः स्वीयम् ऐश्वर्यम् । औत्पत्तिकः स्वाभाविकः ॥४०॥
entries.literal_english: She asks: ‘Is this a dream?’ Looking all around, she rejects that: ‘This is not a dream. Is it then the Lord Hari’s māyā? If so, why do the others not see it? Is it perhaps a delusion of my own mind, like a face seen in a mirror? But how could Kṛṣṇa be perceived within Himself? A mirror does not contain the perception of another mirror. How can the same universe appear both inside and outside? Then there should be a reversal like that between an image and its reflection.’ She then considers another explanation: perhaps there is an inconceivable self-yoga, an innate divine power belonging to me or to this child.

entries.sanskrit: चरमं पक्षम् आश्रित्यायम् ईश्वर इति निश्चित्य् आह---अथो इति । चेतश् चित्तम् । तद्-आदिभिर् न वितर्क-गोचरम् । जगद् यद्-आश्रयं यद्-अधिष्ठानम् । येन करणाधिष्ठात्रा । यतो बुद्धि-वृत्त्य्-अभिव्यक्तात् । नन्व् इदम् अवितर्क्यं भवतु तत्-पदं कीदृक् ? अत आह--सुदुर्विभाव्यम् इति । इदम् अत्यन्तम् अचिन्त्यम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥४१॥
entries.literal_english: Relying on the final explanation, she determines that this is the Lord. The mind and its instruments cannot reach Him by reasoning. He is the support and ground on which the universe rests, and He is known through the intelligence’s illumination by its controlling source. What is that basis like? It is extremely difficult to conceive and utterly beyond thought.

entries.sanskrit: एवं प्रपञ्च-प्रतीत्योन्नीतं तत्त्वं पुनर् जीव-संसृति-हेतु-मायाश्रयत्वेनोन्नयन्त्य् आह---अहम् इति । यशोदा-नामा अहम् असौ मम पतिः । अमुष्य व्रजेश्वरस्याखिल-वित्तपा अहं सती जाया । एष कृष्णो मे सुतः । गोप्य्-आदयश् च मदीया इतीत्थं कुमतिर् यन्-मायया, स एष मे शरणम् इति ॥४२॥
entries.literal_english: From the perception of the universe she now infers the truth as māyā, the support of the jīva’s worldly cycle. ‘I am Yāśodā, this is my husband, I am the wife of the Lord of Vraja, Kṛṣṇa is my son, and the Gopīs and others are mine’—this is the evil understanding produced by His māyā. Yet she concludes, ‘He is my shelter.’

entries.literal_english: Her heart was, as before, filled and made heavy by greatly increased affection.

entries.sanskrit: माया-बलोद्रेकम् आह---त्रय्या इति । त्रय्या कर्म-काण्ड-रूपया इन्द्रादि-रूपेण, उपनिषद्भिर् ब्रह्मेति, साङ्ख्यैः पुरुष इति, योगैः परमात्मेति, सात्वतैर् भगवान् इत्य् उपगीयमानं माहात्म्यं यस्य तम् ॥४५॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord’s greatness is sung in different ways: by the three Vedas in the form of ritual action and as Indra, by the Upaniṣads as Brahman, by Sāṅkhya as Puruṣa, by Yoga as Paramātmā, and by the Sātvatas as Bhagavān.

entries.sanskrit: अति-विस्मयेन पृच्छति---नन्द इति । महोदयं महानुदय उद्भवो यस्य तत् ।
entries.literal_english: With great astonishment she asks about Nanda: ‘What great arising or manifestation is this?’

entries.sanskrit: ययोः प्रसन्नोऽवतीर्णस् तौ पितराव् अपि यं नान्व् अविन्देतां न प्राप्नुताम् । कृष्णस्योदारं महद्-अर्भकेहितं बाल-लीलाम् । यच् च कवयो गायन्ति तद् योऽविन्दत् स किं श्रेयोऽकरोद् इति ।
entries.literal_english: Even the two parents, pleased by whose descent He appeared, did not attain or fully know His generous childhood deeds. What good deed did the poet perform who found and sang those childhood pastimes of Kṛṣṇa?

entries.sanskrit: स एवेह द्रोणो जज्ञे । स च नन्द इति ख्यातः सा च धरा यशोदाभवत् ॥५०॥
entries.literal_english: Droṇa himself was born here and became known as Nanda; Dhara became Yaśodā.

entries.sanskrit: गोप-गोपीनाम् अपि वस्तु-स्वभावाद् अस्त्य् एव भक्तिस् तयोः पुनर् नितराम् इति ॥५१॥
entries.literal_english: The cowherd men and women also possess devotion by their very nature, but in these two—Nanda and Yaśodā—it is especially intense.

entries.literal_english: This devotion arises through the Lord’s own pastime, in which He imitates the role of their son.
